subject: Entitlement rightsize, SLA tradeoffs and economic recap for upcoming renewal
summary: Customer has steady growth (30% QoQ token increase) and burst spikes causing occasional latency blips; proposing a rightsized entitlement + short-term headroom and a blended discount in exchange for 18-month term and modest commit uplift.
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver@latticeai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 spend patterns + renewal check-in (pre-call materials)

Hi Oliver —

Attaching the Q3 token spend breakdown and a short latency profile we pulled for the last 90 days. High-level observations:
- Overall token spend up ~30% QoQ (inference-heavy NLU batch jobs driving most of it).
- Average 99th pct latency for the r-gpt-large model increased from 210ms -> 310ms during two short traffic spikes in Sept (approx 20 min each).
- Prefix caching reduced repeat cost by ~8% on your most active endpoints but burst concurrency still exposes occasional queuing.

For the renewal conversation next week, here are a few items I wanted to get on your radar and ask for quick input on before we propose a formal MA/commit:
1) Rightsizing: would you prefer a conservative base commit + a defined burst pool, or an elevated base to smooth billing predictability?
2) Term length: we can offer a steeper blended discount for an 18-month term vs 12 months.
3) SLA/latency guardrails: we can add an ops playbook and priority routing for a fixed uplift.

Attached: q3_token_spend_breakdown.csv, avg-latency-by-model.pdf, proposed-mop-commit-sheet.xlsx (strawman numbers).

Can you confirm whether procurement will need a PO-first flow or DocuSign is preferred? If possible, share the date range procurement is targeting for signature.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for developers
From: Oliver Chen <oliver@latticeai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 spend patterns + renewal check-in (pre-call materials)

Thanks Mina — useful data, appreciate the ahead-of-time context. A few quick clarifications before our call:

1) Procurement prefers DocuSign but our legal will need to review any SLA addendum.
2) We like the burst-pool idea if it can be isolated (we want predictable overage behavior for our finance team).
3) Can you provide a short ROI example showing cost per effective inference before/after the proposed commit + caching/quantization mix?

Also: our engineering lead (CC'd below in earlier threads) wants assurance that adding a burst pool won’t increase tail latency for our synchronous API calls — is that something Redwood has operationally guarded against?

We’re targeting signature by 2026-11-15 if terms look reasonable.

—Oliver
Oliver Chen
Head of Infrastructure, LatticeAI
oliver@latticeai.com

Date: 2026-10-30T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed rightsize + SLA tradeoffs (strawman)

Oliver — following our call this morning, attaching the strawman economics and a short mutually agreed action plan. Key points:

Proposal snapshot (strawman):
- Base commit: 1.5B tokens / month (current avg ~1.1B) — covers steady-state usage with room for moderate growth.
- Burst pool: 400M tokens reserved (consumed as overage at a known rate) — billed monthly at a predictable uplift.
- Term: 18 months in exchange for 12% blended discount vs current list.
- SLA: 99.9% availability with 95th pct latency target; priority routing and a dedicated escalation path included for uplifts > $X/month (ops add-on).

ROI example (high-level):
- Current blended cost (monthly): $27,000 (token + infra margin)
- Projected blended cost after commit + quantization/KV caching guidance: $21,000
- Net monthly savings: ~$6,000 (22% lower unit economics)

Operational notes on latency and burst pools:
- We will isolate burst capacity on a separate pool with dedicated workers to avoid head-of-line blocking for synchronous endpoints; the burst pool is routed after prefix cache checks and has pre-warmed workers for expected surge windows.
- We’ll include a canary ramp (3 days) and a 48-hour rollback window as part of deployment to validate tail latency during your largest daily windows.

Action items (mutual action plan):
1) Mina: Share final strawman pricing & DocuSign by 2026-11-02. (attached: proposed-mop-commit-sheet.xlsx)
2) Oliver: Confirm DocuSign flow vs PO and provide procurement contact.
3) Karthik/Grace: Prepare a short ops runbook and SLA addendum for LatticeAI to review.

If that aligns, we’ll produce the formal amendment and DocuSign packet.

Thanks — talk soon.
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Oliver Chen <oliver@latticeai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@latticeai.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed rightsize + SLA tradeoffs (strawman)

Mina — this looks reasonable and appreciate the operational detail. Procurement confirms DocuSign is fine (they’ll route the signature internally). A couple of outstanding asks before we sign:

- Can Redwood add a 30-day true-up window for any sustained usage above the burst pool (finance needs predictability)?
- Please include the ops runbook and a one-page technical note that our infra lead can hand off to SRE (we don’t need a deep-runbook, just the escalation steps and expected remediation SLAs).

If you can get the full packet in DocuSign with those two items by EOD 2026-11-05, procurement will route for signatures and we’ll aim for 2026-11-15 completion.

—Oliver
